brief.industry_meta: Video AI · Video Understanding Models / Media Technology
brief.deck: TwelveLabs, the San Francisco and Seoul video-understanding company whose models let broadcasters search footage by what happens in it, closed a $100M Series B on 1 July 2026 co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with Amazon as strategic investor and Red Bull Ventures joining the cap table.
brief.the_case_p1: TwelveLabs announced on 1 July 2026 a $100M Series B co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with Amazon, Radical Ventures, Korea Investment Partners, Index Ventures, Quadrille Capital and Red Bull Ventures, taking total funding to roughly $150M. Amazon made AWS its preferred cloud in a multi-year commitment built on Trainium chips. The money opens offices in New York and London alongside San Francisco and Seoul. Its Marengo and Pegasus models already serve NFL Media and Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, which use them to find exact moments in game footage and package content faster.
brief.the_case_p2: Red Bull Ventures, the group's corporate venture arm launched in 2025 with a €200M fund and led by Nai-Tseng Chen, Red Bull's Global Head of Corporate Finance, calls TwelveLabs its most prominent investment. That is a structural introduction to both Red Bull teams, not a sponsorship. The grid's nearest incumbents are cloud and data platforms, which TwelveLabs runs on rather than against, so the category is a new line on a roster, not a displacement.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 1 July, and the New York and London offices it funds are a brand programme in the two cities where sports media buys technology. Teams set 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter; the United States GP (Austin, October) and Las Vegas GP (November) are the US stages.
brief.why_team_label: WHY VISA CASH APP RACING BULLS
brief.why_team_para: Racing Bulls is the grid's content team: CEO Peter Bayer told Sector that 60 per cent of fans rated its content excellent in F1's latest monitoring report, clear of the field, and its Creator Platform puts young fans to work inside the team. The technology roster is data and observability, Dynatrace and Confluent, with no video-AI partner. Red Bull Ventures already holds TwelveLabs equity, so the introduction exists, and the entry price fits a company that has raised $150M.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO VISA CASH APP RACING BULLS
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Every session produces hours of onboard, garage and broadcast video nobody can search. TwelveLabs indexes it: the content team finds Lindblad's debut points or every Lawson pit stop from one camera in seconds, cuts clips while the session runs, and hands the Creator Platform tagged footage. Engineers get the same search over pit-stop and incident video. In return: a named partnership, livery presence, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Video Intelligence Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the New York and London build-out and the next raise. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year, part-payable in platform usage. Scope: nose or endplate placement, naming of the video-search environment, Creator Platform integration, US hospitality.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Lee co-founded TwelveLabs in 2021 after data-science work at Korea's Ministry of National Defense and a UC Berkeley degree; he fronts every raise. Path: Yoon Kim, President and Chief Strategy Officer since December 2024 (ex-SK Telecom CTO, Apple Siri), and co-founder Soyoung Lee, Head of Business Development. No CMO is listed.

brief.opening_angle_quote: “Jae, Red Bull Ventures backed you a month ago, and its racing teams sit on the most valuable video archive in sport nobody can search. Racing Bulls has no video partner. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 1 July 2026 TwelveLabs announced a $100M Series B co-led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with Amazon as strategic investor, existing investors Radical Ventures, Korea Investment Partners and Index Ventures, and new investors Quadrille Capital and Red Bull Ventures. Total funding is roughly $150M. This is a company release, so the figures are confirmed.

why_now.label: Amazon as preferred cloud
why_now.text: Amazon used the round to make AWS the company's preferred cloud in a multi-year commitment: inference optimised on Trainium chips, new models launching on AWS first. A hyperscaler betting on a video model is the signal that the product has crossed from research into production media workflows.

why_now.label: Offices in the two sports-media capitals
why_now.text: The company is opening offices in New York and London alongside San Francisco and Seoul, and expanding in Los Angeles. Those are the cities where leagues, broadcasters and rights-holders buy technology, and a racing team's content operation is the reference customer that sells to all of them.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US stages on which a San Francisco company would announce, with the Belgian, Hungarian, Dutch and Italian GPs inside the working window for a paid pilot.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Racing Bulls' technology roster is Dynatrace (observability), Confluent (data streaming), Siemens and Randstad, joined in June 2026 by a Salesforce Agentforce deployment for fan engagement and hospitality. Nothing on the roster indexes, searches or understands video. Official Video Intelligence Partner is a new line, not a displacement, and Racing Bulls partnerships are priced below the front of the grid.

why_team.label: The group path
why_team.text: Red Bull Ventures, Red Bull GmbH's corporate venture arm launched in 2025 with a €200M fund and led by Nai-Tseng Chen, the group's Global Head of Corporate Finance, joined the Series B and describes TwelveLabs as its most prominent investment. The introduction to both Red Bull teams therefore exists at group level; the sponsorship still has to be won on product.

why_team.label: The content team of the grid
why_team.text: CEO Peter Bayer says 60 per cent of fans rated the team's content excellent in F1's latest monitoring report, clear of the field. Its Creator Platform has spent two years giving young fans real work inside the team, from a graffiti artist on the São Paulo garage to a designer inside HUGO's studio. A team whose differentiator is content is the team that will use a video-search product every weekend.

why_team.label: Why not Oracle Red Bull Racing
why_team.text: The same group path leads to the senior team, but Oracle's title partnership puts cloud and AI at the centre of that team's story and TwelveLabs has just named AWS its preferred cloud. At Racing Bulls there is no cloud incumbent to argue with, and the entry price matches a company that has raised $150M.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Every session produces hours of onboard, garage, pit-lane and broadcast video that sits in folders nobody can search. Marengo indexes it by what actually happens in the frame; Pegasus writes the metadata. The content team can ask for Lindblad's debut points celebration, every Lawson pit stop from the left camera, or the moment the garage reacts to a result, and cut clips while the session is still running.

value.label: Fuel for the Creator Platform
value.text: The Creator Platform gives young fans real production work. A searchable, tagged archive is the raw material they need, delivered as text queries rather than a media-asset-management training course, which is how the programme scales from a handful of creators to thousands of applicants.

value.label: Engineering review
value.text: The same search runs over pit-stop and incident footage: every stop, every wheel-gun angle, every unsafe release across a season, retrieved by description rather than timestamp. It is the video equivalent of what Dynatrace and Confluent do for the team's data streams.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Video Intelligence Partner designation, nose or rear-wing endplate placement, naming of the team's video-search environment, Creator Platform integration, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, and a racing reference customer for TwelveLabs' New York and London sales teams.
